text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 89:
An eccentric generally used on the crank-shaft for communicating the reciprocating rectilinear motion to the valves of steam engines, and sometimes used for pumping.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 89; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_089.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 95:
On rotating the upright shaft, reciprocating rectilinear motion is imparted by the oblique disk to the upright rod resting upon its surface.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 95; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_095.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 98:
Irregular vibrating motion is produced by the rotation of the circular disk, in which is fixed a crank-pin working in an endless groove cut in the vibrating arm.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 98; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_098.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 118:
A mode of doubling the length of stroke of a piston-rod, or the throw of a crank. A pinion revolving on a spindle attached to the connecting-rod or pitman is in gear with a fixed rack. Another rack carried by a guide-rod above, and in gear with the opposite side of the pinion, is free to traverse backward and forward. Now, as the connecting-rod communicates to the pinion the full length of stroke, it would cause the top rack to traverse the same distance, if the bottom rack was alike movable; but as the latter is fixed, the pinion is made to rotate, and consequently the top rack travels double the distance.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 118; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_118.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 119:
Reciprocating rectilinear motion of the bar carrying the oblong endless rack, produced by the uniform rotary motion of the pinion working alternately above and below the rack. The shaft of the pinion moves up and down in, and is guided by, the slotted bar.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 119; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_119.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 131:
On rotating the disk carrying the crank-pin working in the slotted arm, reciprocating rectilinear motion is imparted to the rack at the bottom by the vibration of the toothed sector.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 131; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_131.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 137:
Expansion eccentric used in France to work the slide-valve of a steam engine. The eccentric is fixed on the crank-shaft, and communicates motion to the forked vibrating arm to the bottom of which the valve-rod is attached.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 137; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_137.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 139:
The internal rack, carried by the rectangular frame, is free to slide up and down within it for a certain distance, so that the pinion can gear with either side of the rack. Continuous circular motion of the pinion is made to produce reciprocating rectilinear motion of rectangular frame.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 139; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_139.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 146:
Continuous rotary motion of the disk produces reciprocating rectilinear motion of the yoke-bar, by means of the wrist or crank-pin on the disk working in the groove of the yoke.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 146; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_146.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 154:
Circular motion into alternating rectilinear motion, by the action of the studs on the rotary disk upon one end of the bell-crank, the other end of which has attached to it a weighted cord passing over a pulley.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 154; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_154.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 158:
Reciprocating curvilinear motion of the treadle gives a circular motion to the disk. A crank may be substituted for the disk.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 158; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_158.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 160:
Alternating curvilinear motion into alternating circular. When the treadle has been depressed, the spring at the top elevates it for the next stroke; the connecting band passes once round the pulley, to which it gives motion.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 160; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_160.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 220:
The two crank-shafts are parallel in direction, but not in line with each other. The revolution of either will communicate motion to the other with a varying velocity, for the wrist of one crank working in the slot of the other is continually changing its distance from the shaft of the latter.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 220; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_220.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 230:
The connecting-rods are so arranged that when one pair of connected links is over the dead point, or at the extremity of its stroke, the other is at right angles; continuous motion is thus insured without a fly-wheel.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 230; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_230.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 362:
Alternating traverse of upper shaft and its drum, produced by pin on the end of the shaft working in oblique groove in the lower cylinder.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 362; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_362.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 374:
Rotary motion of shaft from treadle by means of an endless band running from a roller on the treadle to an eccentric on the shaft.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 374; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_374.html.
